text: You just dropped to your knees with a sharp pain stabbing you in the side.
It started months ago deep inside one of your kidneys.
Your kidneys clean your blood and send the waste out in your pee.
But when you do not drink enough water that waste gets packed too tight.
Tiny bits of calcium and oxalate start sticking together into sharp little crystals.
They stack up day after day into a hard jagged stone.
Then it breaks loose and drops into the thin tube that leads to your bladder.
The stone scrapes the walls and plugs the tube like a cork.
Pee backs up into your kidney and the pain hits in waves.
A small stone can pass on its own but a big one can get stuck.
About one in ten people will get one so drink your water.
Subscribe because that's what's really happening when you get a kidney stone.
